sentence: Knos carries research across the valley of death: each step is paid only on verified proof.

by_hand.note: Counts only a person can supply. Each is changed here, by hand, when the other party agrees to be counted; python scripts/bench_docs.py then writes it into the table of docs/NUMBERS.md.

the price book, Acceptance: 0.30% of a dollar released or reconciled against a signed acceptance, paid by the funder on top; by contract 0.20% of a month's value above 1M, marginal, and never lower; outcomes under 20 USD netted into one release per payee per period with the 0.05 floor once; no cap. It replaces the Settle and Verify lines of the last price book; the row every document and the pricing page repeat (src/knos/billing.py BOOK, tests/data/billing_vectors.json)
facts.has: | Acceptance | dollar released or reconciled against a signed acceptance | 0.30%; by contract 0.20% on monthly value above 1M (the rate never goes below 0.20%); small tickets are netted: outcomes under 20 USD accumulate and settle as one release per payee per period, charged 0.30% of the netted amount with the 0.05 floor once per release; no cap | funder, on top of the amount | knos_pay at release (on chain: 0.30% and the floor; volume rates are a rebate by contract, off chain) |

facts.what: the proposed price book, Meter: an organisation's first 100,000 evaluations in a month free, then 0.002 USD each, from prepaid credits. It is proposed: nobody pays it. The deployed knos_meter on devnet charges 0.05 per evaluation after the first 10,000 of a month, in test USDC
facts.has: | Meter | evaluation | 100,000 a month free per organisation, then 0.002 USD | buyer | prepaid credits |

facts.what: the Meter as deployed: knos_meter on devnet charges 0.05 per evaluation after an owner's first 10,000 of a month, in test USDC (FEE and FREE_PER_MONTH)

the price book, Control, per organisation per year: Team 25,000 USD, Business 100,000, Enterprise from 400,000 (not deliverable yet); a contract price, enforced by nothing on chain; nobody has bought it
facts.has: | Control | organisation, per year | Team 25,000; Business 100,000; Enterprise from 400,000 (not deliverable yet: it needs single sign-on, private deployment and support that do not exist) | buyer | contract |

facts.what: the fee the program takes at release, one rate and a floor, worked by hand in tests/data/billing_vectors.json and by tests/web/price.mjs: 1,000 pays 3.00; 5,000 pays 15.00; 100,000, the most an order holds on devnet, pays 300.00
the price book, Pilot: one buyer and two suppliers for 30 days and one reconciled invoice, 2,500 USD, credited against year one; nobody has bought it and there is no legal entity to invoice from
facts.has: | Pilot | one buyer, two suppliers, 30 days, one reconciled invoice | 2,500 USD, credited against year one | buyer | contract |

facts.what: Intercom's Fin: "From $0.99 per Fin outcome" (Intercom's pricing page)
completed work Bountysource left unpaid, at least (boehs.org, 3 May 2024)

Form 1099-NEC is filed for each person paid at least 2,000 USD in the course of business during the year, for tax years beginning after 2025 (IRS instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC, the IRS's own edition label (12/2026), read 10 Oct 2026)
cheating pull requests in the tamper benchmark (21 ideas in each of three sample repositories), and how many passed plain CI

the price book, Acceptance under a contract: a Plan can lower the program's rate for one owner, to 0.10% at the least (10 basis points; tests/data/billing_vectors.json on_chain.plan_bps_min). No such contract exists

what the program takes at release, shown before funding: fee = max(0.05, floor(amount x 30 / 10,000)); 5 pays 0.05 (1.00%), 20 pays 0.06, 100 pays 0.30, 1,000 pays 3, 5,000 pays 15, 100,000 pays 300 (0.30% each); a release under 16.67 pays the floor. The relayer's tip comes out of the fee

inputs the fuzzer ran against the claim parser in the latest run of program.yml's fuzz job (nightly on main, or by hand on the release branch): `executions` and `source` in the fuzz.json of its `fuzz-claims` artifact. Measured: libFuzzer through cargo-fuzz on the target claims, 300 seconds, commit 511fb84, https://github.com/drexthealpha/Knos/actions/runs/38701807179

the billing rule's volume rates, by contract and marginal: the first 1,000,000 USD of a month's accepted value pays 0.30% and what lies above it pays 0.20%, never less, value released on chain lying first; a proposal nobody has bought (src/knos/billing.py computes it)

the price book, Record: 0.10 USD a lookup of a supplier's delivery record through the machine-priced API, paid per call by the caller; the public record page and its file stay free; the lookup is `knos record serve`, which anyone runs and Knos hosts none of, budgeted at zero revenue. (The last price book's fee for connecting a supplier is gone: connecting a supplier costs nothing.)
facts.has: | Record | lookup of a supplier's delivery record through the machine-priced API | 0.10 USD a lookup, paid per call by the caller (an agent, a marketplace, an underwriter) through the knos-order/x402 flow; the public record page and its file stay free | the buyer, marketplace or insurer reading it | `knos record serve` (anyone runs it; Knos hosts none) |

facts.what: Stripe Billing's pay-as-you-go price: "0.7% of Billing volume" (Stripe's pricing page)

Stripe Billing, pay as you go: 0.7% of billing volume; basic usage-based billing through its Meters API is part of that price, with up to 100M events a month included

the fee on chain follows the build that is live: knos_pay 2.2 charges 0.30% with a minimum of 0.05; knos_pay 2.1, the public program until the upgrade to 2.2 executed on 9 Oct 2026, charged the 0.3.14 fee with a minimum of 0.40, and orders funded under it keep that fee (src/knos/fees.py NEW and OLD)

days of the time lock of the upgrade multisig: 691,200 seconds (192 hours), set by proposal 9, one action SetTimeLock { new_time_lock: 691200 } (docs/reference/GOVERNANCE.md). It executed on 11 Oct 2026, so the lock in force is 8 days; it was 48 hours before
days at most that a proven job's money waits for its payee to bind a wallet (HOLD in knos_pay)
the amounts of the fee's worked examples: 1,000 pays 3.00 and 5,000 pays 15.00, both 0.30% (tests/data/billing_vectors.json, on_chain.fees)
IDT: a Ready brief used 2.08x fewer output (reasoning) tokens than the vague brief of the same task, 20 tasks, one model and effort (scripts/idt_bench.py)
IDT: share of the 20 Ready briefs whose run passed its task's check
IDT: share of the 20 vague briefs whose run passed its task's check
